sense: the mood of a place or a gathering

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.243: hilaritātis plēnum jūdicium ac laetitiae fuit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin has no word for an atmosphere as such: it names the mood that fills a place, as Cicero says a trial was “full of good humour and gladness”. hilaritās is cheerfulness in a person (Cic. Off. 1.108) and, in Columella, fine weather (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Att. 12.40.3: hanc tristitiam temporum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Sadness in a person, and the gloom of times, places and skies (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: itaque hilaritātis plēnum jūdicium ac laetitiae fuit
phrases.english: and so the whole court was full of good humour and gladness

phrases.latin: hilaritātem illam, quā hanc tristitiam temporum condiēbāmus, in perpetuum āmīsī
phrases.english: I have lost for ever the cheerfulness with which we used to season the gloom of these times

sources: Lewis & Short: hilaritas · Lewis & Short: tristitia
